title: Typeset the article
summary: Turn browser-default text into a readable article.
brief: Use the system interface font (system-ui, with sans-serif as fallback) for the whole article.
Keep lines short enough to read: the article is at most 60ch wide and centered in the page.
The title is 2rem with a line-height of 1.15. The intro paragraph (.lede) is 1.25rem. Body paragraphs have a line-height of 1.6.
hints: Set the font once on .article: every child inherits font-family.
max-width: 60ch on .article, and margin-inline: auto (or margin: 0 auto) to center it.
font-size and line-height on the title (.article h1) and on .lede; line-height: 1.6 on .article p. Use a unitless line-height so it follows each element’s size.

children.text: Most readers never notice good typography. They just find the text easy to read.
A comfortable line length, generous spacing between lines and a clear difference between headings and body text do most of the work. None of it needs a special font.
The browser defaults are a starting point, not a design: long lines across the whole window, a serif font and tight lines. A few declarations change that.

solutionNotes: font-family is inherited, so setting it on the article styles every heading and paragraph inside. The ch unit is the width of a "0" in the current font, so 60ch gives roughly 60–75 characters per line whatever the font size. Unitless line-height values are multiplied by each element’s own font size, which keeps the large title tight and the body text airy.
